plugin.name: Cron
plugin.description: See, add and run cron jobs on your hosts, with a schedule preview and the system cron files.

use.title: Use Cron
use.description: See cron jobs on hosts you can reach, and change them on hosts you can edit.

enable.label: Cron
enable.description: Manage cron jobs on this host from the Cron tab.

useSudo.label: Use sudo
useSudo.description: Use sudo for other users' crontabs and /etc/cron.d. Turn off if the login is root.

readOnly.label: Read only
readOnly.description: Show cron jobs but never change them on this host.

tab.title: Cron
tab.error: Could not load cron from this host.
tab.disabled: Cron is turned off for this host. Turn it on in the host settings.
tab.sudo: This needs a root login, passwordless sudo or a saved Sudo Password.
tab.notInstalledTitle: Cron is not installed on this host
tab.notInstalledHint: Install cron or cronie with the host's package manager, then refresh.
tab.notRunning: The cron service is not running, so no jobs will run.

jobs.runDesc: This runs {{command}} once as the crontab's user. It stops after 2 minutes.

form.label: Label
form.labelHint: Saved as a comment above the job.
form.commandHint: Runs with sh in the user's home. A % starts the input cron sends, write \% for a real one.
form.scheduleHint: Minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week, or a word like @daily.
form.scheduleInvalid: This is not a valid schedule.
form.enabledHint: An off job stays in the crontab as a comment.

schedule.monthlyAt: On day {{day}} of every month at {{time}}

raw.title: Crontab as text
raw.hint: One job per line. The host checks the text and keeps the old crontab if it has errors.

system.name: File name
system.nameHint: Saved as /etc/cron.d/<name>. Cron skips names with dots.
system.fileHint: Each job names the user it runs as: minute hour day month weekday user command. Every line is checked before saving.
system.readHint: Some files may be hidden without root. Changes here need a root login, passwordless sudo or a saved Sudo Password.
system.timers_one: This host also has {{count}} systemd timer. The Services plugin manages it.
system.timers_other: This host also has {{count}} systemd timers. The Services plugin manages them.
system.loadFailed: Could not read the system cron files.

logs.noSource: No cron log was found on this host.
logs.failed: Could not read the cron log.

manager.title: Cron
manager.disabled: Turn on Cron for this host in its settings to see its jobs here.

card.title: Cron
card.empty: Turn on Cron for a host to see it here.
